newsitem.title: USA: Texaco officers sued by shareholders over tapes.
newsitem.headline: Texaco officers sued by shareholders over tapes.

text.p: Two Texaco Inc. shareholders sued officers of the oil company Thursday, claiming corporate mismanagement fostered the alleged racist climate at the company that has tarnished its image in the last week.
The suit, filed in federal district court in Manhattan by shareholders Edith Citron and Martin Philip, is what is known as a shareholder derivative action on behalf and for the benefit of Texaco.

The suit is the latest faced by the company after transcripts of a tape recorded in 1994 surfaced recently. The transcripts, in which Texaco executives refered to minority workers as "niggers" and "black jelly beans," were made public last week in a discrimination case filed against Texaco in federal court in White Plains, N.Y.
Texaco has since claimed the words on the tape may be more benign.

Thursday's suit names the current directors of Texaco; Texaco Chairman Peter Bijur; Robert Ulrich, former treasurer; and Richard Lundwall, former senior coordinator of personnel services in Texaco's finance department.

The suit claims the defendants breached their fiduciary duty by their "reckless or grossly negligent failure of the members of the board to adequately inform themselves as to the company's affairs and institute adequate systems of internal control and supervision."
The suit seeks unspecified damages from the 18 defendants.
It seeks to force them to pay Texaco back all their salaries for the relevant period and to pay the damages Texaco may have to pay in the discrimination cases.
A federal prosecutor in New York on Wednesday issued a subpoena to Texaco seeking documents related to racial discrimination allegations by six black employees.
Texaco stock fell 50 cents to $97.50 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
